symptoms: Dark circular spots with concentric rings on older leaves
Yellowing of leaf tissue surrounding the spots
Premature leaf drop starting from the bottom of the plant
Dark, sunken lesions on the stem near the soil line
treatment: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves immediately
Improve air circulation by proper spacing and staking
Water at the base of the plant to keep foliage dry
Apply copper-based fungicides if the infection spreads

symptoms: Small, round to oval orange-brown pustules on leaf surfaces
Pustules break through the epidermis, releasing dusty spores
Chlorosis (yellowing) and premature drying of heavily infected leaves
Reduced kernel weight and spike shriveling in severe cases
treatment: Plant rust-resistant wheat varieties certified for your region
Destroy volunteer wheat plants and weeds that act as green bridges
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization, which favors dense canopy growth
Apply approved triazole or strobilurin fungicides at early stages
